title: Speak No Evil
synopsis: You spent one charming evening with another couple on vacation. They invited you to their country house for the weekend. Every awkward thing you've already overlooked was a warning.

nodes.text: Paddy and Ciara wave from the porch with the warmth you remember. Their house is bigger than they implied. “Be open and grateful” draws you toward The Welcome Drink; “Be polite and observant” leaves The Cottage waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Be open and grateful
choices.consequence: You choose to be open and grateful. By The Welcome Drink, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Be polite and observant
choices.consequence: You be polite and observant. The way toward The Cottage opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Paddy pours something amber. The toast is too long. Your daughter Agnes, nine, drinks her juice carefully and watches their boy Ant, who sits very still on a couch. The distance between Dinner, Course One and Ant's Quiet begins with the choice between “Ask kindly about Ant” and “Move past the silence with a joke.”

choices.text: Ask kindly about Ant
choices.consequence: You choose to ask kindly about Ant. By Dinner, Course One, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Move past the silence with a joke
choices.consequence: You choose to move past the silence with a joke. By Ant's Quiet, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Your guest cottage is across a courtyard. It locks from the outside. Paddy laughs. 'Old farmhouse,' he says. 'Lots of weird quirks.' He shows you a tiny knob to override the latch from inside. The distance between Dinner, Course One and Ant's Quiet begins with the choice between “Use the knob; reset the lock” and “Don't show you noticed.”

choices.text: Use the knob; reset the lock
choices.consequence: You choose to use the knob; reset the lock. By Dinner, Course One, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Don't show you noticed
choices.consequence: You choose to don't show you noticed. By Ant's Quiet, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Ciara serves rabbit. Your wife is vegetarian. Ciara has been told — twice. “Let your wife refuse politely” draws you toward Dance Floor; “Cover for her with a joke” leaves The Bedroom Walls waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Let your wife refuse politely
choices.consequence: Boundaries are also love. You choose to let your wife refuse politely. By Dance Floor, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Cover for her with a joke
choices.consequence: You commit to cover for her with a joke. It carries you into The Bedroom Walls while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Ant doesn't speak. Paddy says he was born without a tongue. He says it like he's offering tea. You notice Ant's mouth opens. You notice the cut is too clean to be congenital. “Quietly text your friend who's a pediatrician” opens the route to Dance Floor. “Try to communicate with Ant directly” changes the terms and carries you toward The Bedroom Walls.

choices.text: Quietly text your friend who's a pediatrician
choices.consequence: You quietly text your friend who's a pediatrician. The way toward Dance Floor opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Try to communicate with Ant directly
choices.consequence: You choose to try to communicate with Ant directly. By The Bedroom Walls, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: After dinner Paddy puts on music too loud. He wants your wife to dance. He grabs her hand. She glances at you. The whole room has, suddenly, the wrong temperature. To choose “Cut in and dance with your wife” means meeting Agnes, Awake; “Politely end the night with a yawn” sends you toward Ciara, Pleading instead.

choices.text: Cut in and dance with your wife
choices.consequence: Intervene physically without escalating. You choose to cut in and dance with your wife. By Agnes, Awake, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Politely end the night with a yawn
choices.consequence: You politely end the night with a yawn. The way toward Ciara, Pleading opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: From the guest cottage you hear, distinctly, Ant crying in the main house. The crying is not normal nine-year-old crying. The crying is muffled because there is a hand over a mouth. Choose “Go to the main house immediately” and Agnes, Awake comes into view; choose “Call the local police first” and the road bends toward Ciara, Pleading.

choices.text: Go to the main house immediately
choices.consequence: You choose to go to the main house immediately. By Agnes, Awake, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Call the local police first
choices.consequence: Authority before action. You commit to call the local police first. It carries you into Ciara, Pleading while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Agnes, in the guest cottage, is awake and afraid. The distance between Back Roads and First Light begins with the choice between “Get the keys and leave tonight” and “Promise her you'll all leave at first light.”

choices.text: Get the keys and leave tonight
choices.consequence: You choose to get the keys and leave tonight. By Back Roads, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Promise her you'll all leave at first light
choices.consequence: Don't drive a back road in the dark. You commit to promise her you'll all leave at first light. It carries you into First Light while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Ciara catches you in the hallway. She is trembling. 'You don't understand,' she whispers. 'We need to leave too. Tonight. Take us with you.' She is, you realize, a victim in this house. The distance between Back Roads and First Light begins with the choice between “Believe Ciara and plan a joint exit” and “Trust nothing yet — get your family out first.”

choices.text: Believe Ciara and plan a joint exit
choices.consequence: You choose to believe Ciara and plan a joint exit. By Back Roads, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Three a.m. The car is loaded. Paddy is at the gate, in the headlights, holding a clipboard like a friendly farmer. He smiles. 'Just a quick question,' he says. The paths divide here: “Drive past him” leads into The Police Station, while “Roll the window an inch and stall” makes The Drive Home the next reckoning.

choices.text: Drive past him
choices.consequence: Don't roll the window down. You choose to drive past him. By The Police Station, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Roll the window an inch and stall
choices.consequence: You commit to roll the window an inch and stall. It carries you into The Drive Home while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Six a.m. The car packed casually. You make it to the gate. Paddy is, somehow, already there, brewing coffee from a thermos. He hands you one through the window. The smell is wrong. The distance between The Police Station and The Drive Home begins with the choice between “Refuse the coffee” and “Take it, pour it out of sight later.”

choices.text: Refuse the coffee
choices.consequence: Don't drink at the line. You refuse the coffee. The way toward The Police Station opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Take it, pour it out of sight later
choices.consequence: You take it, pour it out of sight later. The way toward The Drive Home opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You drive an hour to the nearest town. The constable is, blessedly, alert and skeptical of country charm. You hand over photos, names, and a child — Ant, or Ciara, or both — that you brought with you.

choices.text: Stay to give a full statement
choices.consequence: You commit to stay to give a full statement. It carries you into The Investigation while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Get on the ferry home with your family
choices.consequence: You choose to get on the ferry home with your family. By Therapy, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You drive home with your wife and daughter and, if you took her, Ciara and Ant in the backseat. The morning is, against all odds, blue. Your daughter falls asleep on Ant's shoulder. To choose “Stop at every petrol station to put miles between” means meeting The Investigation; “Drive home in one long stretch” sends you toward Therapy instead.

nodes.text: The local police call colleagues in other countries. Paddy and Ciara have used this trick four times. There are missing families. There are partial confessions. There is finally, finally, a case. “Cooperate fully through the trial” opens the route to Ant's Life. “Give a statement and protect your family's privacy after” changes the terms and carries you toward Five Years Later.

choices.text: Cooperate fully through the trial
choices.consequence: You cooperate fully through the trial. The way toward Ant's Life opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Your daughter starts seeing a therapist who is good with kids. Your wife starts seeing one too. You start, after some resistance, going yourself. The trip becomes, in time, a thing you survived together. Choose “Tell the story when she asks” and Ant's Life comes into view; choose “Don't volunteer until she's older” and the road bends toward Five Years Later.

nodes.text: Ant is in foster care now, with a family that signs. He's twelve. He writes you a letter you frame in a drawer. He says, in clean handwriting, that he is okay. He thanks you for the car ride.

choices.text: Stay in touch as a friend of the family
choices.consequence: You stay in touch as a friend of the family. The way toward The First Visit opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Let him have his new life without yours in it
choices.consequence: You commit to let him have his new life without yours in it. It carries you into The Quiet Decision while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Your daughter, fourteen, asks about it for the first time. You tell her the truth, with edges. She thanks you for taking her seriously that night. You realize that what saved you all was, partly, that you listened to a nine-year-old.

choices.text: Make 'listen to her' a household rule
choices.consequence: The lesson, on the wall. You commit to make 'listen to her' a household rule. It carries you into The Whiteboard while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Just keep doing what you've been doing
choices.consequence: You just keep doing what you've been doing. The way toward The Whiteboard opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Ant's foster parents invite your family for lunch. The house is small and bright and full of signs. Your daughter learns three words on the drive over. The lunch is shy and slow and very, very good.

choices.text: Make this a regular part of your year
choices.consequence: You make this a regular part of your year. The way toward Ant's Aunt opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Send a card next month and see what feels right
choices.consequence: Let the relationship grow at its pace. You choose to send a card next month and see what feels right. By Stepping Back, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You decide what 'stepping back' means in practice — not absence, just not crowding. A card at Yule. A donation to the school he attends, anonymous. You write your role smaller than your heart wants. That, too, is love.

choices.text: Hold to the quiet plan
choices.consequence: You choose to hold to the quiet plan. By Stepping Back, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Make one visit, then decide again
choices.consequence: You make one visit, then decide again. The way toward Ant's Aunt opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: On the kitchen whiteboard you write, half a joke, 'LISTEN TO HER.' Your daughter laughs. Your wife laughs. Then nobody erases it. Six months later it is still there, faded. “Make it the official family rule” opens the route to Listen To Her. “Let it stay faded — habits, not posters” changes the terms and carries you toward Quiet Habits.

choices.text: Make it the official family rule
choices.consequence: Some jokes are also laws. You choose to make it the official family rule. By Listen To Her, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Let it stay faded — habits, not posters
choices.consequence: Some rules are kept by living them. You commit to let it stay faded — habits, not posters. It carries you into Quiet Habits while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Ant calls you on his birthday. He uses a phone with a relay service. You learn enough sign to embarrass yourself. His foster parents become your friends. The story has, somehow, a third family in it that is happy.
You let him build his life without your shadow. You hear, through the lawyers, that he's well. You send a card once a year and hope it lands gently. Sometimes the right amount of help is small.

It becomes the family policy. Agnes uses it on you, the teenager edition. You learn, more than once, that she's right. You raise a daughter who doesn't talk herself out of her own discomfort. That is a quiet revolution.

Your family doesn't make a manifesto out of the weekend. You just live carefully, kindly, with a slightly lower bar for politeness. You hold your wife's hand more often. You take your daughter's instincts more seriously. That, year over year, is the better life.
